mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate sustained liquidity support.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.25%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for three consecutive months, it signals labor market weakness that triggers central bank policy accommodation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as equity valuations benefit from anticipated rate cuts.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0, or average 5-day return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad consumer demand contraction, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings face sector-wide headwinds.
failure_condition: Joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not predict negative 60-day returns (average return not significantly negative, t-test p > 0.05, or Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0) signals manufacturing sector weakness that reduces corporate profit visibility, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors price in economic slowdown risks.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100.0, S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate improving consumer confidence and economic activity, which typically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as housing sector strength signals broader economic expansion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST is rising, or Rank IC < 0.04 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent price pressures that may trigger monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as higher rates compress equity valuations.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL yoy change > 2.5%, S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and declines in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicate labor market deterioration, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as economic contraction risks rise.
failure_condition: Joint condition of UNRATE rising and PAYEMS falling does not predict negative 20-day returns (average return not significantly negative, t-test p > 0.05, or Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth (GDPC1 quarterly growth < 1.0%) indicates late-cycle economic deceleration that typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate earnings growth expectations decline.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 quarterly growth < 1.0%, S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
